headline: Retain the largest k values in a min heap
statement: Return the kth largest value of nums, counting equal values separately. This is position k in a descending sorted sequence, rather than the kth distinct value.
intuition: Keep only the largest k values seen so far in a min-heap. Its smallest value is the current kth largest. A new value matters only if it is larger than that heap minimum. This avoids sorting values that cannot enter the final top k.
approach: Fill a heap with up to k values.
For each subsequent value, replace the root if the value is larger.
correctness: Inductively the heap is the largest k processed values with occurrence count. A smaller incoming value cannot improve this group; a larger one replaces its minimum. The minimum of the final top-k group has exactly rank k.
bruteForce: Sort all values and index the descending result, in O(n log n) time.

complexity.explanation: Heap operations are logarithmic in k and the heap never stores more than k values.

pitfalls: A min heap exposes the item to replace.
